Shankar

For the Petitioner : Mr. Randhir Kumar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Rakesh Ranjan,
A.P.P. For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Kumar Nishant, Advocate Order No. 07 Dated: 09.09.2024

The
petitioner apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections 323/498A/506
(part-1) of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act in connection
with Complaint Case No. 38 of 2023 pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Koderma,
has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the complaint.
The petitioner is the husband of the complainant/opposite party no. 2.
It is further submitted that the petitioner has neither made any demand of dowry nor has tortured the opposite party no.2 for non-fulfilment of the same.
The allegation made against the petitioner in the complaint is completely concocted.
Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
3. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 submits that marriage between the petitioner and the opposite party no. 2 was solemnized in the year 2018.

However, even after marriage, Rs.2,00,000/-
was demanded by the petitioner as well as his family members as dowry from the opposite party no.
2.
The petitioner is also having extra-marital relationship and he threatens the opposite party no. 2 that if the said demand is not fulfilled, he will solemnize second marriage.
Hence, he may not be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
4. Learned A.P.P. also opposes the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering that it is a case under Sections 323/498-A/506 (part-1) of the Indian Penal Code & Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and there is no requirement of custodial trial of the petitioner, without expressing any view on the merit of the present case, he is directed to appear and seek regular bail before the concerned Trial Court within three weeks, which shall be disposed of by the said court in strict compliance of the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021 (10) SCC 773 as well as the observation made in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra) reported in 2023-LiveLaw (SC) 233.
6.

Ritesh/ (Rajesh Shankar, J.)
